title: ADAEZE'S ORCHARD
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: This deliberately returns from pulsar scale to family, soil and public works. It offers the day's most intimate agency test because Adaeze is not an obstacle or a witness but Illuminara's mother, an owner and a better reader of the hillside. The positive outcome is substantial—20,000 people protected while the orchard remains—and can arise from genuine co-design rather than a forced reconciliation.

Draft. Protected: Adaeze's two refusals both change the design; the fractured-bedrock rival is tested and loses on the needle; cancel condition and no-extra-use fallback are stated. Word count is the worker's own count.

A warm, disciplined first draft with unusually strong distributed agency: Adaeze's two refusals alter the engineering, Tomas publicly loses his preferred explanation, Corinna owns the deadline and cancellation threshold, and Idowu supplies the control ground. The 38 m3/s for six hours is internally consistent with the closing 820,000 m3, and the final cost remains visible. The remaining weakness is not the emotional or ethical design but the last causal and hydraulic step: one unspecified needle and a seven-metre strip currently do more proof-work than the prose has earned.

Revision after GPT CRITIC_REVIEW T02. Word count is the worker's own count (about 2,527, slightly over the usual 2,500 because three load-bearing passages were added; scenes 1 and 2 are untouched). Open question recorded, not put to BD: whether a 1-in-400 concrete canal this short would in practice need a full hydraulic report; the story treats Tomas's field check as sufficient under clause 14.

The revision is materially stronger and nearly final. Its best new move is Adaeze's October-flush knowledge: Illuminara's flap solves flood backflow but would slowly destroy the drain, so her mother changes the actual mechanism rather than merely approving it. Tomas's same-stone twin now makes his concession earned, and the five-metre bed, two-metre flow depth and one-metre freeboard give the rescue a readable physical envelope. The remaining weakness is procedural rather than conceptual: Corinna's half-metre freeboard condition is called a cancel condition, but the text does not say when the test pour occurs or explicitly make failure kill the strip alignment before it is relied upon.

Final. Word count is the worker's own (about 2,600, a little over the usual 2,500 because the test pour was added to a story already at its length; scenes 1 to 3 are untouched). Format: dialogue format R1 (scene subtitle first, bold speaker + two spaces + newline, no quotation marks). Open question recorded, not put to BD: whether a short 1-in-400 concrete canal would in practice need a fuller hydraulic report than Tomas's field check; the story treats clause 14 plus the pre-reliance test pour as sufficient.

Illuminara turns a mother's refusal into a falsifiable flood design, lets Adaeze's local knowledge change the mechanism, and earns a dry town through predeclared tests, enforceable consent and visible cost.
